It is one of the five [Nobel Prizes](Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") established by the will of [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") in 1895 and awarded since 1901, the others being the [Nobel Prize in Chemistry](Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), [Nobel Prize in Literature](Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), [Nobel Peace Prize](Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize"), and [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine"). Physics is traditionally the first award presented in the Nobel Prize ceremony.

The first Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to German physicist [Wilhelm Röntgen](Wilhelm_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Röntgen") in recognition of the extraordinary services he rendered by the discovery of [X-rays](X-ray "X-ray"). This award is administered by the [Nobel Foundation](Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") and is widely regarded as the most prestigious award that a scientist can receive in physics. It is presented in <Stockholm> at an annual ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death. As of 2022 a total of 221 [individuals have been awarded the prize.](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics "List of Nobel laureates in Physics")[[2]](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics#cite_note-nobelOrg-2)

**Zhores Ivanovich Alferov** (Russian: Жоре́с Ива́нович Алфёров,  IPA: [ʐɐˈrɛs ɨˈvanəvʲɪtɕ ɐlˈfʲɵrəf]; [Belarusian](Belarusian_language "Belarusian language"): Жарэс Іва́навіч Алфёраў; 15 March 1930 – 1 March 2019) was a Soviet and Russian[[2]](Zhores_Alferov#cite_note-Meissner2019-2)[[3]](Zhores_Alferov#cite_note-Petrova-Koch2020-3) [physicist](Physicist "Physicist") and academic who contributed significantly to the creation of modern [heterostructure physics and electronics](Heterojunction "Heterojunction"). He also became a politician in his later life, serving in the [lower house](Lower_house "Lower house") of the [Russian parliament](Federal_Assembly_(Russia) "Federal Assembly (Russia)"), the [State Duma](State_Duma "State Duma"), as a member of [the Communist Party](Communist_Party_of_the_Russian_Federation "Communist Party of the Russian Federation") from 1995.

Alferov then served as the director of the Ioffe Institute from 1987[[1]](Zhores_Alferov#cite_note-brit-1) to 2003. **Jack St. Clair Kilby** (November 8, 1923 – June 20, 2005) was an American [electrical engineer](Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering") who took part (along with [Robert Noyce](Robert_Noyce "Robert Noyce") of [Fairchild](Fairchild_Semiconductor "Fairchild Semiconductor")) in the realization of the first [integrated circuit](Integrated_circuit "Integrated circuit") while working at [Texas Instruments](Texas_Instruments "Texas Instruments") (TI) in 1958.[[1]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-:0-1): 22 He was awarded the [Nobel Prize in Physics](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics "List of Nobel laureates in Physics") on December 10, 2000.[[2]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-2) Kilby was also the co-inventor of the [handheld calculator](Calculator "Calculator") and the [thermal printer](Thermal_printing "Thermal printing"), for which he had the patents. He also had patents for seven other inventions.[[3]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-IT_Invention-3)

## Early life

Jack Kilby was born in 1923 in Jefferson City, Missouri to Hubert and Vina Freitag Kilby.[[4]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-kshs-4) Both parents had Bachelor of Science degrees from the University of Illinois. His father was a manager at a local utility company.[[4]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-kshs-4) Kilby grew up and attended school in [Great Bend, Kansas](Great_Bend%2C_Kansas "Great Bend, Kansas"), graduating from the [Great Bend High School](Great_Bend_High_School "Great Bend High School"). (Road signs at the entrances to the town commemorate his time there, and the Commons Area at Great Bend High School has been named The Jack Kilby Commons Area.)

Kilby received his [Bachelor of Science](Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree from the [University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign](University_of_Illinois_at_Urbana%E2%80%93Champaign "University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign"), where he was an honorary member of [Acacia fraternity](Acacia_Fraternity "Acacia Fraternity"). In 1947, he received a degree in [electrical engineering](Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering"). He earned his [Master of Science](Master_of_Science "Master of Science") in electrical engineering from the [University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee](University_of_Wisconsin%E2%80%93Milwaukee "University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee") in 1950,[[5]](Jack_Kilby#cite_note-5) while working at Centralab, a division of Globe-Union corporation in <Milwaukee>.

## Career
